approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only accepted scores from the current task. It keeps the best 64 accepted molecules, ordered by score with earlier serials breaking exact ties, and draws breeding parents from the preferred upper half through three weighted score bands. Connected-fragment crossover and bounded chains of atom and bond edits generate a fresh pool. A Gaussian-process model using count fingerprints learns from the complete accepted archive, including discarded survivors, and selects the requested batch through correlated posterior score samples. Canonical identity checks and duplicate rejection connect accepted feedback back to the population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchanges remain disabled.
approach.novelty: Remove only the survivor-capacity truncation: retain every usable accepted molecule in the same score order, then let the original weighted score bands operate on that larger population. This isolates the total contribution of the cap under its existing consumer, including the resulting changes in support and probabilities. Earlier siblings changed recency priority, core competition, recursive breeding, uniform parent allocation, or a recency/uniform combination; none tested this capacity-only removal. We will trace records that the old cap would discard through eligibility, actual breeding and accepted descendants before interpreting the matched endpoint contrast.

observed_bottleneck:
The Parent n-62daf219c70a restricts future graph construction to a bounded score-ranked live cohort even though its predictor retains all accepted labels. Reading all supplied Parent summary.json and run.log files gives a complete three-replica baseline with macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and seed population SD 0.02659287062806747. Read-only reconstruction of its fifteen task logs finds 345 of 435 generation requests with an archive larger than the inherited 64-member capacity, a maximum live size of 64, and all 110295 actual first/partner draws at zero-based ranks at most 31. All 435 archive fits and full fresh pools completed; 4350 accepted offspring yielded 629 strict best-parent beats and 258 incumbent increments. Thus the capacity boundary is naturally encountered, but its endpoint contribution under the original quantile consumer has not been isolated.

Current-Parent references establish why retention, access and useful progress must be separated. In n-8fa256ded991 no directly recency-protected record later entered support or bred, while changed shared-survivor ranks accompanied a -0.011806698456484669 paired mean. In n-2e9e08198747, 182 exposed protected records actually bred, yet the joint recency/uniform mean fell by 0.06516141262576135. Uniform-live n-a56491c332aa and original-support weight removal n-f30747ffdbf8 lost 0.04599801243765703 and 0.05700288256234002 respectively; these preserve the reason to keep the inherited weights, without establishing the cap's sign. Historical core-round n-28dc36ed5be7 also separated protected storage from breeding, but used an older Parent/profile. Those results are distinct controls, not replicated capacity evidence or a decomposition of this total contrast.
hypothesis: Remove only live accepted-population capacity truncation, retaining every usable canonical unique finite-scored accepted record in inherited descending score and ascending serial order for the unchanged score-quantile breeder.

finding_summary.headline: The survivor cap contributed: its removal broadened actual breeding but lowered mean endpoint score by 0.023495
finding_summary.insights:
This answers the narrow capacity question: bounded live membership adds conditional endpoint value when the original weighted score bands, recursive breeding and full-archive predictor remain active. Retained lower-ranked molecules really reached breeding and accepted reuse, so their failure to improve the aggregate cannot be explained by storage without access. The higher parent-win count is not evidence of better search: it accompanies weaker parent references, lower absolute offspring scores and fewer incumbent gains. Evictee-derived products were not uniformly useless—one became its session’s final leader and three improved an incumbent—but those local successes did not offset the total loss.

The audit also identifies the access boundary: merely exceeding 64 live records was insufficient; the original upper-half sampler first exposed discarded ranks when the archive reached 130. This separates the evictee route from earlier probability shifts among shared records. Their individual causal contributions remain unresolved. The frozen molecular assessment found mixed chemistry, with fewer direct nitrogen-halogen bonds but more oxygen-halogen and peroxide bonds, and persistent ring-geometry and stereochemical gaps. Broader breeding therefore did not demonstrate consistently more credible chemistry, nor does that association explain the endpoint loss causally. Whole-loop contribution, chemical mediation, transfer beyond this three-seed profile and any additive relationship to earlier controls remain open; the exact capacity control is answered without a cap sweep.
finding_summary.results:
The removal ran as intended in all fifteen task/seed sessions. Every accepted molecule stayed live, and 1,632 records that the old cap would discard were actually used in 5,005 parent draws. They produced 120 accepted direct offspring; 56 of those later bred and 20 produced another 47 accepted descendants. Eligibility did not guarantee delivery: 289 supported records were never drawn while beyond the old cap, and many batches drew them without accepting an offspring. Probability changes among records already inside the capped population also had substantial exposure, so this is the total capacity effect under the inherited sampler.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.572175, a paired change of -0.023495, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. All three seed macros declined; twelve of fifteen task/seed endpoints declined and three improved. Seed population SD fell from 0.026593 to 0.011713, which does not itself establish reliability. Across accepted proposals, mean absolute score fell from 0.385256 to 0.370365 and the mean best-parent reference fell from 0.470456 to 0.449157. Strict parent wins rose from 629 to 773, while incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 229. All formal sessions completed their full oracle budget.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, heterocycles and aryl amines remain rich, but reactive heteroatom bonds, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: The full Child n-1fdd6af786dc and published Parent n-62daf219c70a Search trajectories were read for every supplied task and seed. All 30 paths exist and contain 300 sequential records, comprising 10 initial and 290 accepted optimizer molecules per task/seed: 4,500 records and 4,350 accepted optimizer proposals per node. All accepted identities are unique within their session, all records parse with RDKit 2023.09.6, and the summaries report no invalid or duplicate emitted attempts. Each initial best, final best, accepted count and terminal best_so_far reconciles with its summary. Regeneration reproduces the immutable Child molecular_digest exactly, including its string counters and excerpts. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with matched seeds 0,1,2 and no profile mismatch. There are no missing trajectory paths, omitted objectives, or absent Child/Parent task/seed chemistry comparisons. These observations describe accepted outputs; unselected fresh-pool proposals and their unobserved rewards are not part of this chemical denominator. The digest final_molecules are the last proposals in its concatenated seed-2 stream, not each seed's best molecule; all per-seed leaders and late streams were inspected separately. Initial molecules are identified as supplied initial observations, not credited as new output. The output contains indole carboxamides, linked carbonyl/thione heteroaromatics, aryl- and cyclic-amine frameworks, quinoline-linked nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. The Child has perceived rings in 4,211/4,350 accepted proposals and aromatic atoms in 4,183/4,350. The digest ring-closure incidences range from 0.9529 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidences from 0.9437 to 0.9793; these are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Ring and aromatic chemistry are rich. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with direct N-halogen bonds in 775/4,350 proposals, O-halogen bonds in 557/4,350 and O-O bonds in 431/4,350, versus 1,042, 278 and 273 in the equally sized Parent output. These overlapping counts do not define a validated synthetic-feasibility score. N-halogen incidence falls while O-halogen and peroxide incidence rise; this is a mixed chemical difference. Conventional carbon-bound halogens and useful nonamide amines are clearly present. RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,098/4,350 Child molecules, versus 2,408/4,350 Parent molecules; no Child molecule has a specified tetrahedral centre or a formally charged atom. Neutral representation does not mean absence of protonatable nitrogen, and no pKa, stereoisomer activity, conformer, synthesis route or stability measurement is supplied. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable and drug-likeness weak overall, despite more plausible individual members. Structural diversity is moderate: many typed and generic graph cores occur, but leading chemistry often stays within related seed-specific families. Typed Murcko cores preserve atom and bond types; generic cores replace atoms by carbon and bonds by single bonds, retaining the extracted graph topology. Their counts neither certify independent pharmacophores nor measure synthetic accessibility. In fixed task order, exact containment of any nonempty initial typed core occurs in 263,5,15,22,18 of 870 Child proposals, while generic-core containment occurs in 533,221,200,163,85. These are subgraph tests, not founder reachability, mapped atom retention or the number of atoms physically conserved through an edit history. Actual atom conservation and multigeneration ancestry are not established by these unmapped trajectory records; they are deliberately not inferred from core overlap. Likewise, chemistry/score associations here do not identify activation, causal chemical mediation or the contribution of the changed population interface. Descriptor definitions, complete row-level measurements, chronological batch summaries, both nodes' per-seed extremes and trajectory/summary SHA256 values are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot2-molecular/audit.json and /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot2-molecular/measured_rows.jsonl. Every cited_smiles entry is an exact Child string from its named task in the immutable request's trusted paths; Parent comparisons use published source coordinates. The highest/lowest decile comparisons below each use 29 of the 290 accepted records per seed, with observed-score ties broken by evaluation order. The prior gap provenance was checked in the indexed published molecular reports for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; this report adds the present paired observations without turning those historical conditions into new component evidence.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted Child proposals were read. RDKit heavy-atom counts span 1-39 (median 25); perceived ring counts span 0-6 (median 3), with median 3 aromatic rings. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko core counts are 247/91 in the Child and 294/123 in the published Parent. The leading families are compact, mostly three-aromatic-ring indole carboxamides connecting a methoxy/alkyl-substituted fused ring to phenyl or pyridyl groups. Seed 0/evaluation 291 is a 24-heavy-atom vinyl/methoxy indole anilide with indole N-F; seed 1/evaluation 273 is a 25-heavy-atom ethyl/methyl/methoxy analogue bearing both amide N-F and indole N-Br; seed 2/evaluation 104 is a 24-heavy-atom indole anilide with an additional five-member oxygen ring and methylamino substituent. The latter has four perceived rings and no N/O-halogen, peroxide or cyclic-cumulene flag. These are chemically recognizable frameworks, but the halogenated nitrogen variants are not ordinary stable substitution patterns. Across the full Child stream, 289/870 contain N-halogen bonds, 11 O-halogen, 10 O-O and 13 a carbon-centred cyclic cumulene. The respective Parent counts are 445,13,5,0. Thus fewer N-halogen structures do not mean all liabilities disappear. In the 29 highest-scoring records per Child seed, nonempty typed/generic cores number 4/1, 4/2 and 8/6; the corresponding Parent counts are 9/6, 2/2 and 9/3. This is real seed variation within closely related leading families, not global scaffold collapse.
liabilities: Indole N-F/N-Br and amide N-F/N-Br replace ordinary nitrogen environments in highly scored molecules; an identical score across F/Br variants does not certify their comparable stability or preparation.

The full stream also contains cyclic peroxides, cyclic cumulenes and very small fragments; 34/870 accepted proposals have at most five heavy atoms. Repeated aromatic substitution dominates many leaders, though chemically less problematic NH amides are present.
missing_features: The high-scoring aromatic-carbonyl/second-aryl arrangement is present. What remains poorly demonstrated is a wider set of chemically credible alternative connectivities that preserves that arrangement; the highest seed-1 family still relies on reactive nitrogen substitution. Seed-0 and seed-2 nonhalogenated relatives are explicit counterexamples to an absolute inability.

The records do not identify a particular absent target pharmacophore or prove a stereochemical requirement. Realizable local bond chemistry and coherent alternative scaffolds are missing assurances, not unobserved objective components that can be named from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Observed final Top-1 values in seed order 0,1,2 are Child 0.4254027310763201, 0.4828171386373609, 0.4188539082916955 and Parent 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596, 0.438972502037081. The supplied starting indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed 0/evaluation 211 keeps an ordinary indole NH and pyridyl amide and scores 0.4239904333396317, close to its seed's 0.4254027310763201 N-F leader. Seed 2's nonhalogenated leader scores 0.4188539082916955. High score therefore does not uniformly require N-halogen bonds. Seed 1/evaluations 273 and 286 exchange amide N-F for N-Br yet share exactly 0.4828171386373609; the score does not distinguish their different bond chemistry. High-decile median heavy-atom counts are 24,26,24 versus 10,8,18 in the low deciles. Small fragments such as seed 1/evaluation 234 cyclic peroxide C1COO1 score 0.0, while the 39-heavy-atom doubled indole at seed 0/evaluation 42 scores 3.861219282660785e-08. The observed gradient is compatible with retaining a compact aromatic-carbonyl/second-ring arrangement, not simply maximizing size or ring count. Late proposals can remain below their earlier best: seed 2/evaluation 300 is an aza-aryl relative at 0.3037868548718482. The Parent seed-0 leader is an N-chloro indole linked through a cumulene/amino segment, seed 1 retains N-F on an indole hydroxylated amide, and seed 2 uses an N-chloro indole diketone; these paired structural differences do not isolate which substituent caused the score differences.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted Child proposals were read. RDKit heavy-atom counts span 1-117 (median 34); perceived ring counts span 0-19 (median 4), with median 4 aromatic rings. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko core counts are 447/308 in the Child and 403/276 in the published Parent. The three seeds develop different N/O-rich aromatic families. Seed 0/evaluation 284 is a 29-heavy-atom, four-ring pair of linked fused nitrogen heteroaromatics with carbonyl, thione, N-alkyl and carbon-bound halogen groups. Seed 1/evaluation 295 is a 36-heavy-atom, five-ring ether-linked heteroaromatic/nitrile framework; RDKit assigns all five rings aromatic, but a triple bond lies in a perceived six-member ring. Seed 2/evaluation 248 is a 35-heavy-atom assembly of methoxy aromatic and aza-aryl units joined through a fluorinated N/O-substituted carbon, carrying a C-S-O-O-F arm and a fused three-member ring. The full output has 25/870 N-halogen, 211 O-halogen, 273 O-O and 44 small-ring alkyne incidences, versus 30,89,218,17 in the Parent. The liabilities are strongly seed-dependent: all 29 highest-decile seed-2 molecules have O-O, 26 have O-halogen, while neither bond occurs in the seed-0 or seed-1 high deciles. The 117-heavy-atom extreme is a highly repeated heteroaromatic/ether construction, not evidence that larger products are better chemistry.
liabilities: The leading seed-1 graph contains a triple bond inside a six-member ring and a bromomethyl ether; aromatic flags and valence acceptance do not establish a persistent, readily preparable compound.

Seed-2 leaders repeatedly contain S-O-O-F/O-O-F or longer oxygen chains, an N/O-substituted fluorinated carbon and fused small-ring geometry. Their local reactivity, stereochemistry and stability are unresolved; 343/870 molecules have RDKit-unassigned centres.

Repeated heteroaromatic elaboration reaches 117 heavy atoms without a corresponding high score, while 25/870 accepted proposals contain at most five heavy atoms. Neither extreme supplies controlled functional context.
missing_features: Linked aromatic nitrogen, oxygen and carbonyl regions are already abundant. The missing demonstrated capability is to preserve useful multi-ring attachment relationships in consistently credible bond and ring environments; the almost equal nonalkyne seed-1 relative shows that at least one such local alternative is reachable.

No Child example reproduces the high observed Parent seed-0 range, but the trajectories do not reveal which unobserved decoration pattern would do so. A specific target-required substructure cannot be inferred from this score gap; source-associated scaffold differences are not evidence for atom conservation or for a causal missing feature.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Observed final Top-1 values in seed order 0,1,2 are Child 0.6020709186382678, 0.6205019253751162, 0.606951871657754 and Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055, 0.6178024026512013. The best supplied initial molecule scores 0.548381482770623. Tiny optimizer structures such as seed 0/evaluation 295 FCCl have the observed floor score 0.5; linked, heteroatom-rich aromatic arrangements attain the higher values. Seed 1/evaluation 275 scores 0.6201180588921683 using a four-ring aza-aryl/ether framework without a cyclic alkyne, almost the same as the six-member-ring-alkyne leader at 0.6205019253751162. This near-equal pair does not establish any need for that difficult unsaturation. Seed 1/evaluation 114, the 117-heavy-atom repeated structure, scores only 0.5630252100840336. The high-decile median heavy-atom counts are 28,34,36, versus 13,27,26 in the low deciles; the size extreme and seed-specific motifs prevent a simple bigger-is-better reading. The Parent seed-0 leader at evaluation 281 has an additional bridged/fused nitrogen ring, O-F and a chloromethyl-ether-containing side chain and scores 0.8561477222467935, above the corresponding Child family's observed range. The Parent seed-1 leader has an aza-aryl nitrile/ether framework with a cyanate group; the Parent seed-2 leader retains peroxide, nitrite and a nitrogen/sulfur group. Hence the Child did not supply a chemically safer analogue of every Parent high-score feature, and the large seed-0 difference does not identify a missing single bond or decoration. The late Child seed-2 evaluation 300 retains O-F/O-O and a strained fused ring but scores 0.588005713994184, below its 0.606951871657754 earlier leader.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted Child proposals were read. RDKit heavy-atom counts span 1-107 (median 30); perceived ring counts span 0-12 (median 4), with median 2 aromatic rings. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko core counts are 406/246 in the Child and 390/258 in the published Parent. High-scoring molecules are aryl-rich amines rather than small sulfonyl fragments: two aromatic regions are joined to saturated nitrogen-containing chains or rings, often with methoxy/phenol and halogen substitution. Seed 0/evaluation 274 is a 26-heavy-atom benzannulated ten-member amine ring with a second phenyl ring, methoxy, aryl F and an N-bromo amino substituent. Seed 1/evaluation 290 is a 31-heavy-atom aryl/partly saturated-ring ether bearing an open polyamine chain, phenol and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 2/evaluation 281 is a 30-heavy-atom bridged aryl-peroxide construction connected to an N-methyl four-member amine ring. Nonamide/nonaryl aliphatic amine proxies occur in 684/870 Child proposals, including ring-associated proxies in 660; the Parent counts are 710 and 688. These are structural nitrogen classifications, not measured pKa values. The generator therefore plainly can make amine centres and saturated nitrogen rings. Full-stream N-halogen/O-halogen/O-O incidences are 67/89/69 in the Child versus 81/93/20 in the Parent. In the high deciles, seed 0 has two N-halogen molecules, seed 1 has none of those three flags, and seed 2 has 16 peroxides. The corresponding high-decile typed/generic core counts are 18/13,15/11,12/11; their variety includes related bridges and ring-size changes, not only peripheral replacements.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader contains N-Br, while seed-2 leaders contain bridged O-O rings and small cyclic amines. Some lower-flag analogues still have saturated carbon-halogen groups and difficult bridged connectivity; absence of the counted flags is not a synthesis certificate.
830/870 Child proposals have unassigned tetrahedral centres and none specify one. The seed-1 leader has two such centres and the seed-2 leader five; the score alone does not resolve their identities.

The full stream includes 28 molecules of at most five heavy atoms and an early 107-heavy-atom, multiply linked acid/amide/sulfonyl structure scoring 0.028858376968164883; both extremes contrast with the compact high-scoring aryl amines.
missing_features: Basic-amine-capable centres are not missing. What is missing is consistently stereochemically specified, geometrically credible aryl/amine assemblies without reactive additions; high-scoring open-chain and nonperoxide examples show that such alternatives are partly reachable.

Charge state, conformer accessibility and stereoisomer identity remain unspecified despite abundant potentially protonatable nitrogen and saturated centres. The supplied scores do not measure which protonation or stereochemical state the objective would reward, so no target-specific amine or ring can be prescribed.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Observed final Top-1 values in seed order 0,1,2 are Child 0.9999981031060403, 0.9909584757406248, 0.9811961806177472 and Parent 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906, 0.9999934235240012. The supplied initial biaryl acid/amide/sulfonamide best scores 0.01904115112334333. Child seed 0/evaluation 16, an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine ketone, scores 0.00021169315013374197; seed 2/evaluation 28 is a small sulfonamide/carboxamide nitrogen ring at 0.0011372896145587985. By contrast, 85 of the 87 highest-decile Child records contain the defined aliphatic amine proxy, and their median heavy-atom counts are 26,31,30. The low-decile median sizes are 19,26,29, so losing the combination of aryl regions, linker geometry and available aliphatic nitrogen matters more descriptively than size alone. Seed 0/evaluation 239 retains a ten-member amine ring and carbon-bound aryl Br, without N-Br, and scores 0.9964674313704724. Seed 2/evaluation 253 has a phenolic aryl/amine framework without peroxide and scores 0.9619658093379853. These counterexamples prevent treating reactive bonds as required for a high score. The Parent seed-0 leader is an open tertiary amine with two substituted aryl groups, seed 1 has a pyrrolidine/aryl-ether polyamine framework, and seed 2 a fused thioether/aryl pyrrolidine; all three Parent leaders lack the Child seed-2 peroxide motif. A late seed-2 water proposal at evaluation 295 scores 0.007584848640642428. The observed scores support the aryl-plus-amine association, but supply no binding pose, protonation measurement or experiment that assigns the score change to an individual feature.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted Child proposals were read. RDKit heavy-atom counts span 1-68 (median 30); perceived ring counts span 0-10 (median 4), with median 3 aromatic rings. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko core counts are 547/372 in the Child and 583/405 in the published Parent. The recognizable chemistry is quinoline- or diaryl-derived aromatic frameworks linked to N-methyl carbonyl-containing rings, with ether, amine, imine and amide/urea-like environments. Seed 0/evaluation 234 has 29 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, including two seven-member N/O-containing rings linked through an exocyclic alkene. Seed 1/evaluation 252 has 32 heavy atoms and a quinoline-linked fused nitrogen/dicarbonyl arrangement with seven- and eight-member rings. Seed 2/evaluation 294 has 29 heavy atoms and a propylquinoline joined to a ten-member unsaturated nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring bearing a carbon-bound chlorine. These families contain ordinary amide and amine substructures, but larger rings, bridges, enamine-like linkages and changing nitrogen environments make route and conformational plausibility case-specific. The full Child stream has 14 N-halogen, one O-halogen and 11 O-O incidences out of 870, compared with 10,0,11 in the Parent. None of the 87 highest-decile Child records has N-halogen, O-halogen, O-O, a carbon-centred cyclic cumulene or a small-ring alkyne. This is an important chemically less reactive counterexample to the other output families. High-decile typed/generic cores number 20/17,22/14,18/13, versus 13/8,21/11,19/10 in the Parent; despite this local high-decile variation the full Child has fewer distinct typed and generic cores than the Parent.
liabilities: Large fused or bridged nitrogen rings and exocyclic unsaturation can be difficult to prepare or conformationally constrained even when no counted reactive bond is present. The high graph-core count therefore overstates neither atom retention nor verified makeable alternatives.

418/870 Child molecules have unassigned tetrahedral centres and none specify a centre. There are also 13 molecules of at most five heavy atoms and a 68-heavy-atom elaboration with a lower score than the initial best; simple fragmentation and growth both lose useful context.
missing_features: Aromatic rings, amide/carbonyl groups and nonamide amines are already present, and the leading deciles avoid several reactive-bond liabilities. The unfilled chemical coverage is credible alternative spatial and connectivity arrangements outside closely related nitrogen/carbonyl ring families that retain their observed useful combination.

Stereochemical identity and conformational/route evidence are absent for the bridged and medium-ring members. The record does not establish that a particular heteroatom, ring count or extra substituent is an objective-required missing feature; small changes near the leaders produce only small and inconsistent score changes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Observed final Top-1 values in seed order 0,1,2 are Child 0.2191149553005537, 0.21700996321176672, 0.22347750788791226 and Parent 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601, 0.22600312875247064. The best supplied initial heterocyclic dicarbonyl scores 0.1678386594791329. Methane at seed 0/evaluation 229 and peroxide OO at seed 1/evaluation 34 score 0.0. The 68-heavy-atom repeated heterocycle/amide example at seed 1/evaluation 26 scores 0.1202735457465673. The high-decile median sizes are 31,31,30 versus 28,30,27 in the low deciles: many lower-scoring molecules are already similar in size, so the useful observation is the arrangement of aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl regions, not added bulk. Seed 2/evaluation 281, lacking the later leader's carbon-bound chlorine, scores 0.2227183003768627 versus 0.22347750788791226 at evaluation 294. Seed 0/evaluation 300 adds a more fused nitrogen/imine arrangement and scores 0.21833203088902578, slightly below its earlier 0.2191149553005537 leader. Related ring and substituent changes occupy a narrow observed high-score interval. Parent leaders preserve the same broad diaryl/quinoline and nitrogen/carbonyl vocabulary, but have different bridged, six-/seven-member or eight-member connections; their endpoint values do not reveal a unique missing target substructure. Chemical simplification and credible alternative placement remain descriptive possibilities, not established score improvements.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted Child proposals were read. RDKit heavy-atom counts span 1-45 (median 26); perceived ring counts span 0-7 (median 4), with median 3 aromatic rings. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko core counts are 230/87 in the Child and 207/92 in the published Parent. The characteristic products are compact fluorinated fused nitrogen heterocycles bearing carbonyl and exocyclic imino groups, with attached phenyl, partially unsaturated carbon rings or small nitrogen rings. Seed 0/evaluation 267 is a 28-heavy-atom four-ring imino/carbonyl heterocycle with N-fluoromethyl, a fluorinated four-member cyclic imine, and a substituted cyclopentadiene bearing a fluoromethyl ether. It has no direct N-F, O-F, O-O or cyclic-cumulene bond, although the four-member imine and unassigned centres remain geometric/identity concerns. Seed 1/evaluation 271 is a 28-heavy-atom dicarbonyl/aryl-amino/cyclopentadiene framework with an N-N(F)F substituent. Seed 2/evaluation 281 is a 26-heavy-atom imino/carbonyl fused heterocycle bearing N-F, fluoroethyl/fluoromethyl groups and an enolic cyclopentadiene substituent. Full-stream Child counts are 380 N-halogen, 245 O-halogen, 68 O-O and 15 carbon-centred cyclic cumulene incidences out of 870; Parent counts are 476,83,19,40. Thus the Child has fewer N-halogen/cyclic-cumulene examples and more O-halogen/peroxide examples. The Child high-decile typed/generic core counts are 15/10,9/5,2/1 versus Parent 7/5,2/1,8/6. Coverage broadens in some seeds and narrows in another; seed 2's leaders share a particularly consistent generic core.
liabilities: N-F, N-N(F)F, O-F and peroxides are frequent, including high-score examples. Carbon-bound F and fluoromethyl ethers must be distinguished from direct N/O-F bonds, since a high-scoring leader contains only the former.

Four-member cyclic imines/alkenes, enolic carbon rings and cyclic cumulenes need geometry and stability assessment. The seed-0 leader has three unassigned tetrahedral centres, the seed-2 leader one, and 436/870 Child proposals have at least one; none specify one.

40/870 accepted proposals have at most five heavy atoms, including 15 after evaluation 200, while the large doubled framework is also near the score floor. The generator does not consistently retain the compact functional context associated with its better scores.
missing_features: Fluorination, carbonyls, imino groups and ring nitrogen are abundant. The missing demonstrated consistency is to combine these features in ordinary local bonding and credible ring geometry across seeds; the seed-0 and seed-2 alternatives without direct N/O-halogen show this is partly achievable already.

Potential stereochemistry, imine/enol tautomeric identity and ring feasibility are unresolved. No absent drug-specific side chain, basic centre or stereoisomer can be inferred as necessary from these trajectories; the score-supported composition/placement association is broader than any such prescription.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Observed final Top-1 values in seed order 0,1,2 are Child 0.687279433418707, 0.4791912195193082, 0.627797445578287 and Parent 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067, 0.7208853668418119. The best supplied initial dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.0020944534688323298. F at seed 0/evaluation 245 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, FF at seed 1/evaluation 110 scores 4.97400031457045e-24, and a 45-heavy-atom doubled imino/carbonyl framework at seed 2/evaluation 135 scores 9.038074984387526e-16. Neither fluorine alone nor duplication of a useful heterocycle preserves the high-scoring configuration. High-decile median sizes are 27,27,24 versus 7,3,23 in the low deciles. The observed useful combination is a compact fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl/imino structure, with important placement and saturation differences, rather than a monotonic fluorine or size count. The seed-0 O-F relative at evaluation 248 scores 0.6083945790955236; its fluoromethyl-ether relative at evaluation 267 scores 0.687279433418707 while avoiding that O-F bond. Seed 2/evaluation 264 also lacks N/O-halogen and peroxide yet scores 0.6104087562395748. Conversely, the seed-1 non-N-halogenated dicarbonyl relative at evaluation 223 scores 0.34753894008990965 versus 0.4791912195193082 for the N-N(F)F leader. These are local observed contrasts, not proof that a bond filter would preserve reward. The Parent seed-0 leader retains N-F and a four-member nitrogen ring, seed 1 a dicarbonyl/phenol fluorinated side-chain arrangement, and seed 2 a five-member cyclic cumulene joined to a nine-member aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring at 0.7208853668418119. The latter Parent geometry is not reproduced by the Child leader; the corresponding lower Child score cannot be treated as a demand to recreate the problematic cumulene. The last Child seed-0 proposal at evaluation 300 rearranges the heterocyclic context and falls to 0.0008414080534947322.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. Among 4,350 accepted proposals, direct N-halogen, O-halogen and O-O bonds occur in 775,557,431 records versus 1,042,278,273 in the equally sized Parent output. The shifts are mixed and counts overlap. Some leaders contain N-Br, N-N(F)F or O-O-F arms; other high-scoring molecules contain ordinary carbon-bound halogens and no such bonds. One fluoromethyl-ether imino/carbonyl leader has no direct N/O-halogen or peroxide, and one complete set of high deciles lacks all three bond types. The gap is conditional local chemistry, not a universal absence of plausible products.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still does not consistently preserve ordinary heteroatom bond environments while modifying otherwise useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need bond-environment-aware alternatives that retain the functional context supported by its own accepted feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens and useful amines from direct heteroatom-halogen and oxygen-chain additions. Evaluate whether chemically ordinary alternatives remain useful rather than assuming a universal filter improves the supplied objective; these structural associations do not attribute the liability to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. The Child has rings in 4,211/4,350 proposals, 35 records with a carbon-centred cyclic cumulene and 44 with a triple bond in an RDKit perceived ring of at most eight atoms. A leader contains a triple bond in a six-member ring; other leaders contain a fused three-member ring, a four-member imine or larger bridged nitrogen rings. A closely scored nonalkyne relative and high-scoring noncumulated structures are present, so unusual geometry is neither universal nor demonstrated to be necessary. Ring/aromatic perception is a graph property, not a conformation measurement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can create many ring graphs without establishing credible cyclic unsaturation, bridge geometry or accessible conformations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic ring transformations need to preserve plausible relationships between ring size, bond order and bridge connectivity while offering alternative arrangements of feedback-supported functional groups. Any geometry check should distinguish ordinary small or fused rings from the particular unsupported unsaturation pattern. No conformer calculations, synthetic routes or score benefit from such a change were established here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,098/4,350 Child proposals and specified centres in none; all supplied stereo-marker and formal-charge string incidences are zero. Individual aryl/polyamine, bridged peroxide and fluorinated cyclic-imine leaders have multiple unassigned centres. Other leaders are achiral by this test. Abundant structural aliphatic amine proxies show that neutral SMILES are not evidence of missing protonatable nitrogen, and a ring or substructure match does not resolve these identities.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves potentially stereogenic molecular identity unspecified after constructing saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations would need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity when the generated chemistry requires it, with appropriate handling of achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation and tautomerism separately. The record establishes an identity gap, not a measured stereochemical reward penalty or a component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. The Child emits 140/4,350 accepted proposals with at most five heavy atoms, versus 123/4,350 in the Parent; small fragments still appear late in every supplied objective stream. Large repeated structures also score poorly: the observed 117-heavy-atom example scores 0.5630252100840336, the 68-heavy-atom example 0.1202735457465673, and the 45-heavy-atom doubled imino/carbonyl example 9.038074984387526e-16 within their separate sessions. Compact multi-region structures outperform both extremes in those same streams, while useful open-chain amines and simpler nonreactive relatives demonstrate that simplification is already possible. Cross-session numerical scales are not pooled into a chemical quality score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful functional context when fragmenting molecules or expanding related ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local accepted feedback to distinguish context-preserving edits from fragment loss and redundant elaboration, keeping enough of the learned functional arrangement while allowing productive simplification. This supports neither a universal minimum size nor a preference for larger molecules. Absence of mapped atom provenance means the needed context cannot be inferred merely from ancestral membership or a retained-core label.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. Per supplied stream, nonempty typed/generic core counts range from 230-547 and 87-372 across 870 Child accepted proposals. Within individual highest deciles they range from 2-22 typed cores and 1-17 generic cores, and several leaders remain close indole-amide or fused imino/carbonyl variants. There are also aryl/amine and nitrogen/carbonyl high deciles with many distinct generic cores, plus different families across seeds: global collapse is false. Relative to the Parent, typed core coverage increases in some streams and decreases in others, while generic coverage can change in a different direction. Exact initial-core subgraphs, generic topology, full-molecule identity, multigeneration ancestry and actual retained atoms are different observations; the latter two are not measured in this molecular audit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many graph identities do not yet establish a broad set of independent, chemically credible alternatives to the leading family within each search.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Seek chemically plausible scaffold rearrangements that preserve feedback-supported functional relationships and assess useful alternatives beyond peripheral substitutions. Track typed and generic core coverage separately and validate geometry and local chemistry rather than rewarding string novelty alone. Use atom-mapped edit evidence for any future retention claim; neither founder reachability nor core overlap supplies it. These observations motivate a coverage question, not a claim that diversity necessarily improves scores or that the changed population rule caused the gap.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
